data.narrative:
Xcimer Energy is a Series A-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $100M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 entities spanning the nuclear energy sector: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Fuse Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy. The peer set spans from Seed through Series B stages.

Two valuation methods triangulate to a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis, applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yields $200M based on the $100M total raised as a proxy baseline. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A)—produces a median of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The median valuation across both methods is $504M, with a triangulated range of $170M to $929M.

Key uncertainties include stage-appropriateness of the peer set; Valar Atomics' Series B valuation of $6.0B materially widens the comp range. The stage-progression method's conservatism relative to peer-median implies either that Xcimer's Series A positioning commands below-market multiples or that peer valuations reflect sector-specific momentum not yet reflected in later-stage progression norms. Capital efficiency and technology de-risking remain critical valuation drivers pending further funding rounds.
